text: 居委会张大妈：听说你们家小赵失业啦？
en: Auntie Da Zhang from the residents' committee: I hear your Xiao Zhao is out of work?

text: 残疾啦？
en: Disabled?

text: 高位截瘫？
en: High-level paraplegia?

text: 哦，家庭生活困难？
en: Oh, so the family is in financial difficulty?

text: 我们居委会都听说啦。
en: Our residents' committee has heard all about it.

text: 这不，给她安排一个名额，营业执照都办好了，在你们家营业就行。
en: So we've arranged a spot for her—the business licence is already sorted—and she can just run it from your home.

text: 工作很轻松，不用怎么动弹，嘴能张开，舌头能动就行。
en: The work is very easy; she won't need to move about much—just being able to open her mouth and move her tongue will do.

text: 四近的邻居都可以来消费嘛，回头咱在小区楼下办一促销活动，充两千送八百。
en: Neighbours all around can come and spend, you know. Later we'll run a promotion downstairs in the estate: top up two thousand and get eight hundred free.

text: 我跟物业说说，小区里那么多保安都可以消费嘛。
en: I'll have a word with the property management; there are so many security guards in the estate who can all come and spend.

text: 你们也在业主群里宣传，让楼上楼下邻居都来。
en: You should also spread the word in the owners' group chat and get the neighbours upstairs and downstairs to come too.

text: 刚开始要是生意实在不好，我让我家老李，还有我那儿子都过来照顾生意。
en: If business is truly slow at the start, I'll get my Lao Li and my son to come and patronise.

text: 没事，国家鼓励的，收入也挺高。
en: It's all right—the state encourages it, and the income is quite high.

text: 哪啊，多少健康孩子还托关系找我呢。
en: Not at all—plenty of healthy youngsters even pull strings to get to me.

text: 这可是准入行业，执照不好办。
en: This is a licensed trade; the permit isn't easy to obtain.

text: 这也就是帮助残疾人就业，是残联和咱街道上给咱家孩子的一个关怀。
en: This is simply helping disabled people into work—a kindness shown to our child by the Disabled Persons' Federation and our subdistrict office.

text: 对，要感谢领导。
en: Quite right, we must thank the leaders.

text: 一句话可以爆杀他们：
en: One sentence can utterly demolish them:

text: 开补习班都不合法的地方，要是卖淫合法，多少有点违背常理。
en: In a place where even running a tutoring class is illegal, if prostitution were made legal, that would be rather against common sense.

text: 打开你的手机，打开手机中的录音。
en: Take out your phone and open the voice recorder on it.

text: 然后问问这位支持卖淫合法化的，他会不会支持自己的老妈，老婆和女儿去从事这个行业？
en: Then ask this person who supports legalising prostitution whether he would support his own mother, wife and daughter entering this line of work?

text: 如果他回答不会，那么他凭什么支持合法化？
en: If he says he would not, then by what right does he support legalisation?

text: 如果他回答会，那么请把录音转发给他老婆，女儿和老妈听。
en: If he says he would, then please forward the recording to his wife, daughter and mother to listen to.

text: 你找父母要钱时:你怎么能不管我！
en: When you ask your parents for money: 'How can you just not care about me!'

text: 你玩游戏时:你怎么能管我！
en: When you play games: 'How can you control me!'

text: 卖淫嫖娼时:这是自由！
en: When it comes to prostitution and soliciting: 'This is freedom!'

text: 性病人口贩卖:这是政府无能！
en: STDs, human trafficking: 'This is government incompetence!'

text: 这完美诠释了伪自由主义者对政府的态度。
en: This perfectly illustrates the attitude of pseudo-liberals towards the government.

text: 果然，大多数人根本不理解自由主义与功利主义之间不可调和的矛盾，以及这个矛盾背后所反映出来的最基本的常识。
en: As expected, most people simply fail to understand the irreconcilable contradiction between liberalism and utilitarianism, and the most basic common sense that this contradiction reflects.

text: 自由主义的核心是:人是自己的主人，人可以做任何事情，只要不伤害到别人的自由。
en: The core of liberalism is this: a person is master of themselves, and a person may do anything, so long as it does not harm the freedom of others.

text: 这个核心逻辑下，卖淫，器官买卖，吸毒（只说吸，不谈所引起的犯罪），死刑（没人有资格杀死别人，哪怕他杀了人），堕胎（胚胎是不是人），反对阶梯税率，反对福利政策，小政府主义，都可以在这里找到理由。
en: Under this core logic, prostitution, organ trading, drug use (speaking only of use, not of the crimes it gives rise to), the death penalty (no one is entitled to kill another, even if that person has killed someone), abortion (is an embryo a person), opposition to progressive tax rates, opposition to welfare policy, and minimal-government doctrine can all find their justification here.

text: 其实，在这样的核心逻辑下，整个社会更接近被“文明人”批判的“社会达尔文”体系。
en: In fact, under such core logic, the whole of society draws closer to the 'social Darwinism' system that 'civilised people' criticise.

text: 每个人为自己负责。
en: Each person is responsible for themselves.

text: 对待别人的“侵犯”，自己才是第一责任人，你不够强，你不够聪明，你不够勤劳，你不够背景，活该你被淘汰，社会不会为你自己的缺陷去买单。
en: In the face of others' 'encroachment', you yourself are the first responsible party. If you are not strong enough, not clever enough, not hard-working enough, not well-connected enough, then you deserve to be eliminated—society will not foot the bill for your own failings.

text: 而功利主义的核心:人是社会性的，人不完全是自己的主人，个人需要负担社会（族群）责任，社会（族群）也要负担对个人的责任。
en: And the core of utilitarianism: a person is a social being; a person is not entirely master of themselves. The individual must bear responsibility towards society (the ethnic group), and society (the ethnic group) must also bear responsibility towards the individual.

text: 这个核心逻辑下，大政府主义，贸易壁垒，种族主义，以及对应自由主义的反向操作，都可以在这里找到理由。
en: Under this core logic, big-government doctrine, trade barriers, racism, and the reverse of liberalism's measures can all find their justification here.

text: 当然，会有人反驳，没有国家是完全的自由主义或者功利主义的。
en: Of course, some will object that no country is wholly liberal or wholly utilitarian.

text: 是的，因为人都是很“贱”的存在，一方面我们想接受好处，另一方面却又不想付出代价。
en: Indeed, because human beings are a rather 'base' sort of existence: on the one hand we wish to receive the benefits, yet on the other we are unwilling to pay the price.

text: 所以，所有的社会政策都是在两种主义之间的缝合，裁剪，妥协。
en: Thus all social policy is a matter of stitching together, tailoring and compromising between the two doctrines.

text: 可是，在两种主义背后，一个原则是不会变的:
en: Yet behind the two doctrines there is one principle that does not change:

text: 得到多少，失去多少。
en: You gain only as much as you lose.

text: 任何政策的好处，都是拿其它地方的坏处换的。
en: The benefits of any policy are purchased with the ills elsewhere.

text: 你要从父母手上拿钱，那就接受父母对你的管教，服从他们的安排。
en: If you would take money from your parents, then accept their discipline and submit to their arrangements.

text: 你当然有权力不接受他们的管教，那你也没有权力要求他们为你付出。
en: Of course you have the right not to accept their discipline—but then you have no right to demand that they spend on your behalf.

text: 你可以要求卖淫合法化，但是你就不能强求那些裸贷，贫困，吸毒，未成年等带来的“不那么让人舒服”的卖淫被遏制，因为甄别“自愿”与“强迫”是需要极大的社会成本的。
en: You may call for prostitution to be legalised, yet you cannot then insist that the 'rather uncomfortable' forms of prostitution—those arising from nude loans, poverty, drug use, minors and the like—be curbed, because distinguishing 'voluntary' from 'forced' demands an enormous social cost.

text: 同样，既然社会收回了普通人“自甘堕落”的权力，那么社会就有义务为弱势群体，无能力者供养，再就业培训，脱贫，义务教育。
en: Likewise, since society has taken back ordinary people's right to 'degrade themselves of their own accord', society has the duty to provide for the vulnerable and the incapable, to offer re-employment training, to alleviate poverty, and to provide compulsory education.

text: 每一条基因的存在，都是淘汰无数同类基因后表达下来的，
en: The existence of every single gene is expressed only after countless kindred genes have been eliminated,

text: 每一次进化，都是在无数种族中艰难挣扎而出的，
en: and every step of evolution emerges only through the arduous struggle among countless species,

text: 你要得到多少，就要失去多少。
en: As much as you would gain, so much must you lose.

text: 这知乎的风气真是越来越迷了，在恋爱话题下，哪个女生要是聊聊自己过去的恋爱史，那评论区可就要炸开锅了，一群男的涌进来diss人家答主，我还寻思看样子知乎的主流是保守主义啊。
en: Zhihu's atmosphere really grows more and more bewildering. Under topics about romance, whenever some girl mentions her past relationships a bit, the comments section goes into uproar—a swarm of men pour in to diss the answerer. I had thought, going by appearances, that Zhihu's mainstream was conservatism.

text: 可现在画面转到卖淫的话题，怎么一个个的又支持卖淫了？
en: Yet now the scene turns to the topic of prostitution, and how is it that they one and all support prostitution again?

text: 这还算是保守主义吗？
en: Does this still count as conservatism?

text: 想融入知乎主流是真难啊，舆论走向左右横跳的太厉害了，想找一个稳定的立场实在不容易。
en: Fitting into Zhihu's mainstream is truly hard; public opinion lurches left and right far too violently, and finding a stable standpoint is really no easy matter.

text: 我看评论区有些人误会了，我并没打算讨论该不该合法的问题，对此我也不感兴趣，我想指出的是，“女人必须守身”和“我支持卖淫合法”，这两点加在一起，就等于“女人必须守身，我可以随便嫖”，这显然很无耻。
en: I see some in the comments have misunderstood. I never meant to discuss whether it ought to be legalised, nor am I interested in that. What I wish to point out is that 'women must preserve their chastity' together with 'I support the legalisation of prostitution' adds up to 'women must preserve their chastity, yet I may freely visit prostitutes'—which is plainly shameless.

text: 评论区有人指出，持有这两个观点的不是同一伙人，但我认为双方的重叠程度不低，首先提出“女人必须守身”，并在网上随便攻击陌生人的群体，显然他们的攻击性是很强的，且认为要求陌生人给自己的观念买单是理所当然的，根本没有尊重陌生人性自由的概念，那么对于这样的一群人来说，女性可以合法的卖淫，符合他们要求的女性应该守身的观念吗？
en: Some in the comments have noted that those holding these two views are not the same crowd, but I think the overlap between the two sides is considerable. The group that first advances 'women must preserve their chastity' and casually attacks strangers online clearly has a very strong aggressiveness, and takes it for granted that strangers should pay for their own ideas, with no notion whatsoever of respecting strangers' sexual freedom. For such a group, then, does women being able to prostitute themselves legally accord with their demand that women ought to preserve their chastity?

text: 这显然是强烈冲突的，那么一群攻击性这么强，又不尊重陌生人自由的群体，为什么从来没网暴过支持卖淫合法的群体呢？
en: This is plainly a fierce contradiction. So why is it that a group so aggressive, and so disrespectful of strangers' freedom, has never once cyberbullied the camp that supports the legalisation of prostitution?

text: 因为他们突然又变得尊重他人自由了吗？
en: Is it because they have suddenly learned to respect others' freedom?

text: 你信吗？
en: Do you believe that?

text: 对于这样区别对待的情况，身为一个社会人，我只能理解为，卖淫合法的主张，其实并不违背这群人的真实想法，显然想强迫女性守身的群体，仅仅只是想让女性单方面守身而已，但自己并不愿接受性保守的约束，那么很明显的，他们之所以到处攻击素不相识的陌生女性不守身，其动机纯粹就是出于封建式的物化女性罢了。
en: Faced with such unequal treatment, as a member of society I can only understand it this way: the call for prostitution's legalisation does not in fact run counter to this group's true thinking. Clearly, the group that wishes to force women to preserve their chastity merely wants women to preserve their chastity unilaterally, yet is itself unwilling to accept the restraints of sexual conservatism. It is thus obvious that their motive in attacking total strangers—unfamiliar women—for not preserving their chastity, everywhere and at will, is purely the feudal objectification of women.

text: 那么就得出了个很有意思的结论，最封建的一群人，也是女性最想远离的一群人，反而把自己装作了婚恋市场的主力军，不得不说真是滑稽的现实，越是局外人，bb的倒越凶。
en: We thus arrive at a rather interesting conclusion: the most feudal crowd of people—the very crowd women most wish to keep their distance from—instead cast themselves as the main force in the marriage market. One has to say this is a truly farcical reality: the more of an outsider one is, the louder one's bb becomes.
